conceptCapsule.title: Kinematics of Rotational Motion
conceptCapsule.summary: 1. Angular Variables: Angular displacement $\theta$, angular velocity $\vec{\omega} = \frac{d\vec{\theta}}{dt}$, and angular acceleration $\vec{\alpha} = \frac{d\vec{\omega}}{dt} = \omega\frac{d\omega}{d\theta}$. 2. Vector Character: Finite angular displacements are not vectors (non-commutative under addition), whereas infinitesimal angular displacements $d\vec{\theta}$ and $\vec{\omega}$ are axial vectors directed along the axis of rotation given by the right-hand thumb rule. 3. Vector Kinematic Links: $\vec{v} = \vec{\omega} \times \vec{r}$, $\vec{a}_t = \vec{\alpha} \times \vec{r}$, and $\vec{a}_r = \vec{\omega} \times \vec{v} = -\omega^2 \vec{r}$. Net linear acceleration is $a = \sqrt{a_t^2 + a_r^2} = R\sqrt{\alpha^2 + \omega^4}$. 4. Constant $\alpha$ Equations: $\omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t$, $\theta = \omega_0 t + \frac{1}{2}\alpha t^2$, $\omega^2 = \omega_0^2 + 2\alpha\theta$, and $\theta_n = \omega_0 + \frac{\alpha}{2}(2n - 1)$.
conceptCapsule.examTrap: Remember that $\vec{v} = \vec{\omega} \times \vec{r}$ requires the vector cross product in proper order; $\vec{r} \times \vec{\omega} = -\vec{v}$. Also, whenever $\alpha$ is given as a function of $\theta$, do NOT use $\alpha = \frac{d\omega}{dt}$; instead use the chain rule relation $\alpha = \omega\frac{d\omega}{d\theta}$ to integrate directly.

questions.statement: The angular displacement of a rotating wheel varies with time as $\theta(t) = 2t^3 - 6t^2 + 10\text{ rad}$. The angular acceleration of the wheel becomes zero at time $t$ equal to:
questions.solution:
$$\omega(t) = \frac{d\theta}{dt} = 6t^2 - 12t, \quad \alpha(t) = \frac{d\omega}{dt} = 12t - 12$$
Setting $\alpha(t) = 0 \implies 12t - 12 = 0 \implies t = 1\text{ s}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A wheel starts rotating from rest with a uniform angular acceleration of $4\text{ rad/s}^2$. The total angle turned by the wheel in the first $5\text{ seconds}$ is:
questions.solution:
$$\theta = \omega_0 t + \frac{1}{2}\alpha t^2 = 0 + \frac{1}{2}(4)(5^2) = 2 \times 25 = 50\text{ rad}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: Which of the following quantities in rotational kinematics is an axial vector?
questions.solution:
Angular velocity $\vec{\omega}$ is an axial vector directed along the axis of rotation via the right-hand thumb rule. Finite angular displacements do not commute under vector addition, while moment of inertia is a tensor/scalar and kinetic energy is a scalar.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A flywheel rotating at $1200\text{ rpm}$ slows down uniformly to $600\text{ rpm}$ in $10\text{ seconds}$. The number of revolutions completed by the flywheel during this time interval is:
questions.solution:
Initial frequency: $N_1 = 1200/60 = 20\text{ rps}$; Final frequency: $N_2 = 600/60 = 10\text{ rps}$.
$$n = \left(\frac{N_1 + N_2}{2}\right)t = \left(\frac{20 + 10}{2}\right)(10) = 15 \times 10 = 150\text{ revolutions}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The position vector of a particle rotating in a circle of radius $r = 2\text{ m}$ is $\vec{r} = (2\hat{i})\text{ m}$ and its angular velocity vector is $\vec{\omega} = (3\hat{k})\text{ rad/s}$. The linear velocity vector $\vec{v} = \vec{\omega} \times \vec{r}$ of the particle is:
questions.solution:
$$\vec{v} = \vec{\omega} \times \vec{r} = (3\hat{k}) \times (2\hat{i}) = 6(\hat{k} \times \hat{i}) = 6\hat{j}\text{ m/s}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A rigid body rotates with an angular velocity $\omega(t) = (4t - 3)\text{ rad/s}$. The total angular displacement between $t = 1\text{ s}$ and $t = 3\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
$$\Delta\theta = \int_1^3 (4t - 3) dt = \left[2t^2 - 3t\right]_1^3 = (18 - 9) - (2 - 3) = 9 - (-1) = 10\text{ rad}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: For a particle executing circular motion of radius $R$ with angular speed $\omega$ and angular acceleration $\alpha$, the magnitude of the net linear acceleration is:
questions.solution:
Radial component: $a_r = R\omega^2$; Tangential component: $a_t = R\alpha$.
$$a_{\text{net}} = \sqrt{a_r^2 + a_t^2} = \sqrt{(R\omega^2)^2 + (R\alpha)^2} = R\sqrt{\omega^4 + \alpha^2}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A motor rotates at a constant speed of $\omega = 30\text{ rad/s}$. When switched off, it comes to rest after completing $45\text{ radians}$ under constant angular retardation. The magnitude of the angular retardation is:
questions.solution:
$$\omega^2 = \omega_0^2 - 2\alpha\theta \implies 0 = 30^2 - 2\alpha(45) \implies 90\alpha = 900 \implies \alpha = 10\text{ rad/s}^2$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A particle moves along a circle of radius $R = 0.5\text{ m}$ such that its speed increases at a constant rate $a_t = 3\text{ m/s}^2$. The angular acceleration $\alpha$ of the particle is:
questions.solution:
$$a_t = R\alpha \implies \alpha = \frac{a_t}{R} = \frac{3\text{ m/s}^2}{0.5\text{ m}} = 6\text{ rad/s}^2$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: If the angular acceleration of a wheel is related to its angular velocity as $\alpha = -k\omega$ (where $k$ is a positive constant), the angular velocity after time $t$ from initial speed $\omega_0$ is:
questions.solution:
$$\frac{d\omega}{dt} = -k\omega \implies \int_{\omega_0}^\omega \frac{d\omega}{\omega} = -k\int_0^t dt \implies \ln\left(\frac{\omega}{\omega_0}\right) = -kt \implies \omega(t) = \omega_0 e^{-kt}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A ceiling fan is rotating at $120\text{ rpm}$. When the power is turned off, it completes $20\text{ revolutions}$ before coming to a stop with uniform deceleration. The time taken to stop is:
questions.solution:
$$\omega_0 = 120 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = 4\pi\text{ rad/s}, \quad \theta = 20 \times 2\pi = 40\pi\text{ rad}$$
$$\theta = \left(\frac{\omega_0 + \omega}{2}\right)t \implies 40\pi = \left(\frac{4\pi + 0}{2}\right)t = 2\pi t \implies t = 20\text{ s}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The angular acceleration of a body rotating about a fixed axis is $\alpha = 3t^2\text{ rad/s}^2$. If it starts from rest at $t = 0$, its angular displacement at $t = 2\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
$$\omega(t) = \int_0^t 3t^2 dt = t^3, \quad \theta(t) = \int_0^t t^3 dt = \frac{t^4}{4}$$
$$\theta(2) = \frac{2^4}{4} = 4\text{ rad}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A particle moves in a circle of radius $r = 1\text{ m}$. Starting from rest, it is accelerated at a constant angular rate $\alpha = 2\text{ rad/s}^2$. The time at which the magnitude of radial acceleration equals the magnitude of tangential acceleration is:
questions.solution:
$$\omega(t) = \alpha t = 2t \implies a_r = r\omega^2 = 1(2t)^2 = 4t^2, \quad a_t = r\alpha = 1(2) = 2$$
$$a_r = a_t \implies 4t^2 = 2 \implies t = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\text{ s}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The ratio of the angular speed of the second hand to that of the hour hand of a standard mechanical clock is:
questions.solution:
$$T_s = 60\text{ s}, \quad T_h = 12 \times 3600 = 43200\text{ s}$$
$$\frac{\omega_s}{\omega_h} = \frac{T_h}{T_s} = \frac{43200}{60} = 720 : 1$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A wheel rotates with an angular speed $\omega = (2\theta + 5)\text{ rad/s}$, where $\theta$ is in radians. The angular acceleration $\alpha$ when $\theta = 5\text{ rad}$ is:
questions.solution:
$$\alpha = \omega\frac{d\omega}{d\theta} = (2\theta + 5)(2)$$
At $\theta = 5\text{ rad}$: $\alpha = (2(5) + 5)(2) = 15 \times 2 = 30\text{ rad/s}^2$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: Two gears $A$ and $B$ are in mesh. The radius of gear $A$ is $r_A = 10\text{ cm}$ and that of gear $B$ is $r_B = 25\text{ cm}$. If gear $A$ rotates with an angular speed of $50\text{ rad/s}$, the angular speed of gear $B$ is:
questions.solution:
Tangential linear speeds must match at contact: $$r_A \omega_A = r_B \omega_B \implies \omega_B = \frac{r_A \omega_A}{r_B} = \frac{10 \times 50}{25} = 20\text{ rad/s}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: An infinitesimal angular displacement $d\vec{	heta}$ is treated as a true vector because:

options.text: It has both magnitude and direction
It obeys the commutative law of vector addition ($d\vec{	heta}_1 + d\vec{	heta}_2 = d\vec{	heta}_2 + d\vec{	heta}_1$)
It is always perpendicular to the linear velocity
Its magnitude is measured in radians

questions.solution:
Vector quantities must obey commutative vector addition. Finite rotations do not commute ($\theta_1 + \theta_2 \ne \theta_2 + \theta_1$), but infinitesimal angular displacements do commute ($d\vec{ heta}_1 + dvec{ heta}_2 = d\vec{ heta}_2 + d\vec{ heta}_1$).
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A wheel starts from rest and accelerates uniformly with $\alpha = 4\text{ rad/s}^2$. The angular displacement during the $3\text{rd second}$ of its motion is:
questions.solution:
$$\theta_n = \omega_0 + \frac{1}{2}\alpha(2n - 1) = 0 + \frac{1}{2}(4)(2(3) - 1) = 2(5) = 10\text{ rad}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A point $P$ on the rim of a rotating disc of radius $R = 0.2\text{ m}$ has a linear speed of $v = 4\text{ m/s}$ and net linear acceleration of $a = 80\sqrt{2}	ext{ m/s}^2$. The angular acceleration $\alpha$ of the disc is:
questions.solution:
Centripetal acceleration: $a_r = \frac{v^2}{R} = \frac{4^2}{0.2} = 80\text{ m/s}^2$.
Total acceleration: $a^2 = a_r^2 + a_t^2 \implies (80\sqrt{2})^2 = 80^2 + a_t^2 \implies a_t = 80\text{ m/s}^2$.
$$\alpha = \frac{a_t}{R} = \frac{80}{0.2} = 400\text{ rad/s}^2$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A shaft rotating at angular speed $\omega_0$ is subjected to a retarding angular acceleration $\alpha = -c\sqrt{\omega}$. The time required for the shaft to come to complete rest is:
questions.solution:
$$\frac{d\omega}{dt} = -c\sqrt{\omega} \implies \int_{\omega_0}^0 \omega^{-1/2} d\omega = -c \int_0^t dt \implies \left[2\sqrt{\omega}\right]_{\omega_0}^0 = -ct \implies t = \frac{2\sqrt{\omega_0}}{c}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.
